purpose: Preview concepts for existing ERSRR research viewer

artifacts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one polished, high-fidelity desktop application UI concept image for ERSRR, a university methane satellite research project. Landscape 16:10 composition, approximately 1920x1200. Full application screenshot, front-on, crisp legible text, no physical device or presentation border. This is the first of two connected screens, the national overview. Focus on excellent daily research usability, restrained professional dark UI with shadcn-style controls, excellent contrast, no decorative dashboard cards or marketing content.

Visual system: near-black charcoal #111619 shell, subtly lighter #192125 panels, off-white text, readable muted secondary text, thin #303c43 dividers, 6px corner radius controls, clean Inter-like sans serif, monospaced coordinates. Teal #53c6bd only for active controls. Cyan means reference annotation; orange means model prediction. Amber and coral are reserved for model score markers. No neon glow, gradients, glassmorphism or science-fiction HUD.

Layout: compact full-width top bar with small understated ERSRR symbol and name at left, breadcrumb Research / Map, tabs Map active, Compare, Imagery, Experiments. Right side: outlined button 'Open experiment viewer ↗', small 'Design concept' badge. Beneath, a usable research workspace: left 265px sidebar for filters and scene list; center dominant map canvas occupying about 62% width; right 300px selected-scene inspector. Bottom of map, slim acquisition date scrubber and compact scale/navigation. Map is the visual anchor, lots of breathing space.

Map: correctly proportioned geographic map of the contiguous United States with subtle state boundaries, dark desaturated relief, legible sparse state labels, muted ocean. Alaska and Hawaii insets in lower left. Keep the US entire silhouette visible. Show a small cluster of saved scenes around southeastern New Mexico / West Texas, a selected outlined diamond near latitude 32.134 N longitude 103.982 W, a muted input-only marker at Volusia Florida, and an input-only marker in Georgia. These are sparse research observations, NOT nationwide detection coverage; do not scatter dozens of invented confirmed events. Selected southwest marker has a subtle teal selection ring and little scene-footprint rectangle. A small map caption says 'Saved observations • unmarked areas have no result'. Include zoom plus/minus, home extent, satellite/basemap toggle, layers.

Left sidebar labels, clean rows not floating cards: 'Find a location or scene', date filter 'All dates', 'Model / experiment' dropdown 'All saved experiments', 'Review status' filter. Then 'Saved scenes' with small thumbnail rows: selected 'Permian Basin' / '01 Nov 2023 · Model6 R5' / 'Partial detection'; 'West Texas' / '04 Jun 2023' / 'Missed plume'; 'Volusia, Florida' / '01 Jun 2025' / 'Input only'. Other simple rows 'Negative control' / 'False positive' and 'Georgia' / 'Input only'. Colored status chips have text and not just color. Bottom count 'Diagnostic sample'.

Right inspector: 'Permian Basin', subtitle '32.134° N, 103.982° W', '01 Nov 2023'. Model dropdown 'Model6 R5 · Mean', small amber label 'Experimental'. Large compact real-looking desert satellite thumbnail with roads and a narrow cyan reference contour and an imperfect orange predicted plume over the same area. Label thumbnail 'Illustrative preview'. Beneath short aligned facts: 'Scene IoU 38.8%', 'Evaluated area 19.36%', 'Run IoU 2.15%'. Quiet line 'Run failed quality gate'. Primary full-width teal action 'Open in experiment viewer ↗'; secondary 'Compare here'. Use no invented physical methane quantities or confidence probability. 'Show image footprint' checked, reference / prediction layer toggles. Compact legend cyan Reference, orange Prediction, gray No output. The figure is a UX design concept, imagery is illustrative.

Timeline along bottom of center map: sparse date ticks 2023, 2024, 2025 and observed acquisitions, not a fake live time series. A tasteful segmented control 'Map / Satellite' at top of map. Tooltips and selection must not obscure US geography.
Overall feel: serious, calm, beautiful research instrument that connects a national map to an existing local experiment viewer. Excellent information hierarchy, practical touch/click targets, readable 14-16px equivalent labels. Avoid dense tiny text, summary KPI tiles, huge logos, meaningless charts, promotional copy, unsupported success claims, and any Discord elements.
artifacts.correctionPrompt:
Edit the provided ERSRR US map concept. Preserve the layout, US map, palette, typography, right inspector, primary actions, scene metrics and visual hierarchy exactly. Make ONLY a targeted correction to sample metadata text so inputs are not wrongly attributed to a trained model:
1. Sidebar Volusia, Florida row: replace '01 Jun 2025 · Model6 R5' with '01 Jun 2025 · EMIT intake'. Keep 'Input only'.
2. Sidebar Negative control row: replace its date/model line with 'Saved review example'. Keep 'False positive'.
3. Sidebar Georgia row: replace its date/model line with 'EMIT intake'. Keep 'Input only'.
4. Right inspector bottom Scene ID value: replace invented 'ERSRR_20231101_103982' with 'MARS …8207778b'.
Do not move or restyle any other component. This remains a design concept with illustrative cartography and satellite preview.

artifacts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Generate one high-fidelity desktop application interface concept, full-screen front-facing screenshot, landscape 16:10 approximately 1920x1200, for ERSRR methane research software. This is the scene comparison state of the same calm dark map-first research app. Primary UX: start from a US map, select a geolocated satellite scene, compare source imagery against reference annotation and a saved model result, then optionally open the existing full experiment viewer in a separate browser tab. Do not draw a hardware device, promotional landing page, dashboard KPI card grid, or multiple disconnected mockups.

Consistent visual language: charcoal #111619 frame, slightly lighter #192125 work surfaces, crisp thin dividers #303c43, off-white text and high-contrast secondary gray, teal #53c6bd selection and primary button, cyan reference contour, orange prediction overlay, gray diagonal hatching outside valid output. Restrained shadcn-like components, compact clear sans-serif typography, monospaced coordinates, 6px corners, minimal icons, clean generous alignment. No glow, no gradients, no cyberpunk. Every panel useful.

Top bar 64px: ERSRR at left, Research / Compare breadcrumb; tabs Map, Compare selected, Imagery, Experiments. Right an outlined button 'Open experiment viewer ↗' and a tiny 'Design concept' badge.
Second context toolbar: back arrow 'Back to US map', scene title 'Permian Basin', exact date '01 Nov 2023', coordinates '32.134° N, 103.982° W', scene switcher arrows. Small 'Reused development scene' label.
Thin toolbar below: model dropdown 'Model6 R5', branch segmented options 'Mean' selected, '16', '32', '64', '128'; comparison mode options 'Side by side' selected and 'Swipe'; checked 'Link pan & zoom', 'Reset view', and compact overlay opacity slider. Make these affordances legible with comfortable spacing, not crowded.

Primary workspace occupies 65% of height: three large equal square satellite panels aligned horizontally, absolutely matching scale, view bounds, road intersections and landmarks.
Panel 1 header 'Sentinel-2 RGB', subtitle 'Target acquisition'. Plausible arid Permian basin farmland/oil access roads satellite imagery with dusty tan earth and sparse green vegetation. Panel 2 header 'Reviewed reference', subtitle 'MARS plume annotation', exact same imagery and same coordinates under a narrow elongated cyan plume outline. Panel 3 header 'Saved prediction', subtitle 'Model6 R5 · Mean', exactly same imagery with an orange prediction region that only partly overlaps the cyan reference contour, visibly imperfect. The outer area of all three panels is softly muted with diagonal hatching; only central 44% of each image width/height is fully active to reflect central 19.36% area coverage. Important do not make the output look perfect. All three show a shared small crosshair, 200 m scale bar, and consistent north indicator. Directly beneath all three one quiet sentence: 'Illustrative imagery • linked geographic extent • hatched area has no model output'.

Lower workspace is an efficient shallow split tray. Left 25% has a small locator map around the New Mexico / Texas border, state boundary labeled, selected teal image footprint rectangle and location pin with coordinates. Label 'Location' and a clear 'Show on US map' text link. Middle 45% is a compact scene results and provenance region with simple divider-separated aligned text, not separate cards: 'This scene' then 'IoU 38.8%   Precision 64.4%   Recall 49.3%', 'Valid comparison area 19.36%', 'Reference: MARS reviewed plume', 'Acquired: 01 Nov 2023'. Right 30%: 'Whole experiment', '65 development scenes', 'Pooled IoU 2.15%', small muted amber 'Failed quality gate' status, then primary teal button 'Open in experiment viewer ↗', one short supporting line 'Keeps this scene and experiment selected'. A bottom strip allows 'Mark for review', 'Add note', 'Export view' with concise labels.
Small bottom-right legend: cyan Reference, orange Prediction, hatched No output. Keep scene metrics visually separate from experiment metrics. Do not call scores physical methane concentration, emission rates, or calibrated confidence. No invented model training completion. This is a design concept, not experimental evidence. No Discord.
The result should feel like an exceptionally well-designed scientific instrument, map-aware, useful for long research sessions, rich enough for actual work, visually polished but honest and highly legible.
